content.user_title: Build Azure Blob Storage Java Apps
content.value_statement: Java developers need precise Azure Blob Storage examples for common SDK tasks. This skill provides focused snippets for clients, containers, blobs, streaming, SAS tokens, and metadata.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for Azure Storage Blob SDK for Java.
Provides examples for BlobServiceClient, BlobContainerClient, and BlobClient creation.
Covers blob upload, download, streaming, copy, delete, and listing patterns.
Explains SAS token generation for blob and container access.
Includes metadata, HTTP header, lease, proxy, and error handling examples.
limitations: Does not validate live Azure credentials or storage account permissions.
Does not generate a complete production application structure.
Does not cover every Azure Storage service outside Blob Storage.
Examples use placeholders that developers must replace securely.

use_cases.title: Add Blob Features
use_cases.description: Add upload, download, and listing features to a Java service using Azure Blob SDK patterns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Azure Integration
use_cases.description: Plan container access, metadata, SAS tokens, proxy settings, and environment variables for Blob Storage.

use_cases.title: Review SDK Workflows
use_cases.description: Compare common Blob SDK workflows before writing implementation guidance for a Java team.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Upload
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, explain how to create a BlobClient and upload text to Azure Blob Storage in Java.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Streaming Transfer
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, outline a Java approach for uploading and downloading large blobs with streams and overwrite control.

prompt_templates.title: Design Secure SAS Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, design a Java pattern for read-only blob SAS generation with a one-day expiry and minimal permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this skill, compare client creation, proxy configuration, metadata handling, leases, and error handling for a production Blob Storage service.

output_examples.input: Help me upload a local file to Azure Blob Storage from Java.
output_examples.output: The response describes BlobClient creation, file upload with overwrite choice, and credential placeholders to replace securely.

output_examples.input: I need a read-only SAS for one blob.
output: The response recommends blob-level read permission.
It notes a short expiration and secure token handling.

output_examples.input: How should I stream large data to Blob Storage?
output_examples.output: The response explains stream upload, input stream cleanup, and download stream handling.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential when possible.
Keep SAS permissions narrow and expiration times short.
Replace placeholders with secret management, not hardcoded credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not commit connection strings, SAS tokens, or account keys.
Do not grant write or list permissions when read access is enough.
Do not treat example paths and container names as production defaults.

faq.question: What Azure library does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure Storage Blob SDK for Java package.

faq.question: Can it help create BlobServiceClient objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows creation with SAS tokens, connection strings, and DefaultAzureCredential.

faq.question: Does it include upload and download examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes text, file, stream, and output stream examples.

faq.question: Does it explain SAS token generation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes blob-level and container-level SAS token examples.

faq.question: Can it verify my Azure account settings?
faq.answer: No. It provides coding guidance, but it does not inspect live Azure resources.
